message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights and obligations you should know: | Category | Tenant Rights | Tenant Responsibilities | |----------|---------------|-------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent (or two if the lease is for a furnished unit).
• Landlord must return the deposit within 30 days after the lease ends, minus any lawful deductions.
• Landlord must provide a written itemized statement of deductions. | • Keep the property clean and free of damage beyond normal wear and tear.
• Provide proper notice before moving out (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month leases). | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a habitable condition (plumbing, heating, structural integrity, etc.).
• Tenants can withhold rent or repair and deduct if the landlord fails to address major repairs. | • Report maintenance issues promptly in writing.
• Follow reasonable instructions for repairs (e.g., schedule times for access). | | **Entry & Privacy** | • Landlord must give at least 24 hours’ written notice before entering, except in emergencies.
• Entry is allowed during reasonable hours unless otherwise agreed. | • Cooperate with scheduled entry times.
• Keep the premises accessible for inspections. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease agreements are required for leases longer than one year.
• Lease terms cannot violate public policy or be unconscionable. | • Sign a lease only after reviewing all terms.
• Pay rent on time and in the manner specified. | | **Discrimination** | • Protected against discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (including public assistance). | • Provide truthful information when applying for housing. | | **Rent Control & Eviction** | • No statewide rent control; local ordinances may apply.
• Landlords must follow the eviction process: serve a notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment), file a complaint, and obtain a court order. | • Respond to notices promptly.
• Attend court hearings if served. | | **Utilities & Repairs** | • Landlord must provide essential services (heat, hot water, electricity, plumbing).
• If utilities are not provided, the tenant may pay and then recover costs from the landlord. | • Pay utilities if responsible per lease.
• Avoid tampering with utility meters. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenants have the right to use the premises without unreasonable interference. | • Respect neighbors and avoid disruptive behavior. | ### Practical Steps for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Look for clauses about security deposits, maintenance responsibilities, and notice periods. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications with your landlord, photos of any damage, and receipts for repairs you perform. 3. **Know the Notice Requirements** – For month‑to‑month leases, a 30‑day written notice is typically required to terminate. 4. **Report Issues Promptly** – Send written notices (email or certified mail) for any maintenance problems. 5. **Seek Legal Advice if Needed** – If you believe your landlord is violating your rights, consult a local attorney or tenant advocacy group. If you need a specific document—such as a lease agreement template or a notice of termination—you can let me know, and I can generate it for you.
